title: The Harris Bluebird in Virginia, where musicians jammed until morning
summary: The Bluebird across the bridge stayed open until 5 or 6 a.m. and was where D.C. musicians went to jam in the late 1930s.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Sure. Then later on, John went out to the Bluebird, a place called the Harris Bluebird. That was out across the bridge, too.

Yeah. It stayed open until 5 or 6 o'clock in the morning. They'd be out there jamming then. That's where everybody went every night to go jam. All the musicians, when they get through here in town, would go out there.
What year would this have been?
